question: Is Cheniere's Stage 2 tape strong enough to override a Downtrend market and compressed valuation?

web_blocks.html: The S&P 500 trades in a confirmed Downtrend with 34.5% of stocks above their 50-DMA, 10 distribution days, and only 3 of 11 sectors above their 50-DMA [40][42]. Against that weak backdrop, Cheniere acts as a rare relative-strength leader. On November 20, 2026, LNG closed at $294.84 (-0.18% daily, -4.51% weekly in market facts / -5.79% in TradingView). Its 63-day relative strength stands at +14.65% and 28-day relative strength at +14.10% versus the S&P 500 [38][42].

Both the market-facts ledger and the TradingView snapshot classify LNG in Stage 2 (Markup) with zero split between feeds [38][42]. Price sits +1.17% above its 10-week EMA ($291.43) and +2.97% above its rising 50-day SMA ($286.33). It also holds +10.43% above its 30-week SMA ($267.00) and +12.02% above its 200-day SMA ($263.21) [38][42]. Weekly RSI sits at 55.31, Daily RSI sits at 49.63, and 4-Hour RSI stands at 44.91 below the 4H 20-EMA ($298.95), keeping intraday_4h_turn = false [42].

web_blocks.title: OVERRIDDEN BY DOSSIER VERDICT: Why We Stand Aside on the $280/$400 Bull Call Debit Spread
paragraphs: OVERRIDDEN BY DOSSIER VERDICT: The automated options block below (#options-overlay) prints the pre-refresh 54-DTE January 15, 2027 $280/$400 Bull Call Debit Spread at $24.99 ($2,499 max loss) with a pre-ratchet $278.52 stop. Although 41.2% implied volatility sits below 51.1% 20-day realized volatility, the trade requires LNG above $304.99 just to break even in 54 days and caps profit at $400. That conflicts with our Pass 2 $315.00 Base fair value, REJECTED new-capital verdict, and ratcheted $281.56 stop, so we stand aside.

web_blocks.html: Our stop-loss ratchet protects existing shares without forcing an early sale. The scanner snapshot lists a deeper 30-week stop at $262.23 [38]. Lowering our stop from $278.52 to $262.23 would violate our upward-only ratchet rule. Instead, we trail the stop up to $281.56, set half an ATR ($4.77) below the rising 50-day SMA ($286.33) and just beneath Pivot S1 ($282.97).

Technical Trigger: A daily or weekly close below $281.56 on heavy volume breaks the 50-day SMA ($286.33) and Pivot S1 ($282.97), forcing an exit of all 6.2472 shares; reclaiming the 4H 20-EMA ($298.95) opens a test of $315.00–$325.00.

book_paragraphs: Even when a business looks fully priced on normalized cash flow, we always inspect the price chart before making a portfolio decision. Selling a strong Stage 2 leader too early is costly, just as buying an overvalued stock late in a cycle is dangerous.

On November 20, 2026, Cheniere's chart shows clear strength against a weak market. The S&P 500 sits in a confirmed Downtrend with ten distribution days and just 34.5% of stocks above their 50-day averages. Yet Cheniere closed at $294.84, beating the index by 14.65 percentage points over 63 sessions.

Both our daily ledger and TradingView classify Cheniere in Stage 2 Markup. Shares rest 1.17% above the 10-week EMA at $291.43 and 2.97% above the rising 50-day SMA at $286.33. Pullback volume ran light at 0.81 to 0.92 times normal, signaling normal digestion.

Two technical limits still stand out. First, 4-hour RSI sits at 44.91 below a falling 4H 20-EMA at $298.95, so short-term buyers have not turned higher. Second, our upward-only stop ratchet blocks lowering our prior $278.52 stop to the scanner's $262.23 30-week floor.

Instead, we trail our held stop up by $3.04 to $281.56, half an ATR below the rising 50-day average and just under Pivot S1 ($282.97). That sets the closing-trigger distance at 4.5% below today's close, though overnight Hormuz de-escalation headlines at 51.1% realized volatility can still gap past $281.56. At the same time, upside from the $295.80 support top to $315.00 ($19.20) versus $14.24 of stop risk equals just 1.35-to-1, failing our 1.50-to-1 hurdle for new money.

book_subsections.title: OVERRIDDEN BY DOSSIER VERDICT: Why We Skip the Automated Options Spread
paragraphs: Our options scanner flagged cheap implied volatility—41.2% option pricing versus 51.1% realized volatility—and proposed a January 2027 $280/$400 bull call spread for $2,499. The volatility math is accurate, but an option spread must match the equity thesis.

With 54 days to expiry and a $304.99 breakeven, that spread bets on a fast rally past our $315.00 normalized fair value inside a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend. We keep stocks and options aligned by rejecting fresh equity and skipping new call spreads.

book_callouts.title: THE UPWARD-ONLY STOP RATCHET
book_callouts.text: On held Stage 2 winners, stops ratchet upward behind rising intermediate averages ($278.52 to $281.56 behind the $286.33 50-day SMA), never downward. That keeps held risk small while letting the trend prove itself.
